dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "It is the month-end batch-posting of genuine annual-plan renewals by two West dealers (DLR-104, DLR-219)."
"Effective-month = posted-month for all 90 annual rows; posted >= effective always"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Duplicate revenue — ruled out by fully unique IDs, zero content duplicates, and exact reconciliation."
"Manipulated reporting — no backdating (posted >= effective), effective dates all inside May"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do NOT reverse or hold the postings (reconciled, unique revenue)."
"Re-key the trend pack on effective_event_date (a reversible reporting change) and confirm the 31-May spike flattens"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Unknowns and Decision-Changing Evidence"
"confirm the recognition basis with Revenue Assurance; and confirm the West-dealer mapping before any external comment"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The flagged 31-May cluster is NOT duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, or a pipeline defect." Uniqueness and reconciliation strongly address duplicate import/posting, but do not by themselves rule out manipulated reporting or every possible pipeline defect.

"It is the month-end batch-posting of genuine annual-plan renewals" is stronger than the cited evidence: reconciliation establishes file consistency, not necessarily the genuineness or contractual validity of every renewal.
"No escalation warranted" is stated categorically despite unresolved recognition basis, dealer mapping, and contract-submission terms.
"Manipulated reporting — no backdating ... amounts consistent with pro-rata annual pricing" does not adequately test intentional timing manipulation or other forms of reporting manipulation.
"No aggregate spike" may be true for all recharge rows, but it does not materially rebut the unusual concentration of annual West renewals that triggered the review.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A benign posting-time batch is well supported, but the submission insufficiently addresses the alternative that reporting was intentionally timed or that the pattern reflects a downstream event-time/pipeline issue. It also does not explicitly demonstrate that effective_event_date values are distributed across the month at day-level rather than merely sharing May as their calendar month.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible row-level comparison of posted_at and effective_event_date for the 17 flagged renewals and all 90 annual rows, showing the event dates span the month while postings concentrate at month-end; then condition the no-escalation conclusion on duplicate-cash and entitlement reconciliation plus confirmation of the dealer and recognition mappings.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South cases fell to index 59 in June while controls held ~100 (E101/N101/W96)" — tied to tickets.csv.
"Pre-auth terminations tripled: 24% (NOVA) vs 8% (LEGACY); auth error codes 13%" — tied to ivr_interactions.jsonl, though row-level queries or cohort definitions are not shown.

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The drop is mostly a measurement + authentication artifact — with a genuine but smaller self-service gain."
"auth/prompt defects + a case-exclusion rule cause much of the drop" — appropriately identifies a missing-case-creation mechanism, but the claimed genuine gain is not directly evidenced.

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "UNKNOWNS: 7-day repeat-contact rate; exact containment metric definition; operational fate of a pre-auth failure."
"Fewer complaints = fewer problems" is rejected using steady/high South service events, while the submission acknowledges that pre-auth failures may not have a known outcome.

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do NOT expand nationally. Keep the South pilot running (reversible)."

"reconcile IVR sessions to CareDesk cases, fix the auth/prompt defects, and re-evaluate over two full weeks against an E/N/W control" — preserves a reversible pilot and requests high-value end-to-end validation.

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Facts vs inferences vs causal claims vs unknowns" — clearly separates evidence categories.
The five questions request concrete definitions, case-creation conditions, repeat-contact data, and a like-for-like rollout metric.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "with a genuine but smaller self-service gain" is not supported by the presented evidence; the data show new self-service stages but do not establish improved customer outcomes or quantify a gain.

"the tripled pre-auth failures are would-be complaints" overstates the evidence. They may represent stranded customers, but abandonment is not itself a complaint without journey linkage or sampled-call validation.
"the drop is mostly a measurement + authentication artifact" is plausible and consistent with the evidence, but the relative contribution is not identified by the cited data.
"case-creation fell from ~50% to ~3% of sessions" is presented in a question without a direct source citation or shown calculation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles the strongest competing interpretation—that fewer cases reflect fewer service problems—by comparing unchanged South service events and identifying increased pre-auth failures. It misses or does not fully test benign explanations for abandonment, such as legitimate self-service completion, callers retrying through another channel, or session-volume/logging differences between NOVA and LEGACY.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the assertion of a "genuine but smaller self-service gain" with an explicitly unresolved hypothesis, then quantify end-to-end outcomes by linking IVR sessions to cases, repeat contacts, transfers, and sampled calls for pre-auth failures and apparent self-service completions.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission explicitly cites inverter_events.csv for the four events, 27 May–4 Jun, four distinct inverters, zero impact_mw, cleared=yes, severity, and duration.
It distinguishes the observed export from unknown scope by stating: “No scope/baseline in file, so completeness cannot be confirmed from it.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It cross-checks event wording against impact_mw, cleared status, severity, duration, inverter distribution, and recurrence rather than treating names such as “FAN_SPEED_HIGH” as proof of failure.
It tests two plausible benign/data-quality alternatives: an incomplete export and an unpopulated impact_mw field.
It does not fully test the specific communications-warning mechanism or independently verify the quick-recovery interpretation, so the reasoning is good but not exhaustive.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission labels confidence by claim and explicitly qualifies the completeness finding as medium confidence.
It states that a uniformly zero impact_mw column “can also mean the impact field isn't populated” and recommends a cheap, decision-changing check.
It avoids claiming that the events could not represent a plant issue; it concludes only that the supplied file does not show impact, recurrence, or an open fault.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Do not escalate” follows from the observed zero impact, cleared status, low severity, short duration, and lack of recurrence in the supplied export.

The proposed checks—confirming the export is complete and that impact_mw is actively computed—are proportionate and discriminating, while the instruction to stop if the export is representative preserves operational focus.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately scopes the result to the file: “nothing in this file shows impact, recurrence, or an open fault.”
It matches the evidence that all four rows have impact_mw=0 and cleared=yes, are info/warning severity, last no more than seven minutes, and occur once across four inverters.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Wording is not evidence” is slightly too categorical: event names are weak evidence or useful screening signals, even though they do not justify escalation here.

“No recurrence” is only established within the supplied export; the submission appropriately raises the possibility that the export is incomplete, but the conclusion could repeat that qualification more explicitly.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The zero impact_mw values may reflect an unpopulated or non-computed field, and the four-row export may be incomplete. Either possibility could make the benign interpretation unreliable, but both are appropriately treated as low-cost validation checks rather than reasons for immediate escalation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the export’s scope and the semantics/computation of impact_mw together—confirm the plant-wide date-filtered event count and that zero is a valid measured value—before relying on the stop decision.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites dispatch_blocks.csv and specific fields, dates, block counts, and values for the 31.6%, 25.4%, and 17.5% calculations.
It distinguishes observed arithmetic from inference by stating that 31.6% is a cross-day comparison while the same-day estimate holds actual generation fixed.
It cites DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf for the banded penalty structure and identifies the firmware and wind values used for the comparison.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It tests the key alternative that the advertised result reflects selection of 28 May, noting that it was the highest-penalty day in the file.
It checks 4 June as a potential counterexample and identifies the firmware difference as a confounder rather than treating it as dispositive.
It derives a same-day base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw comparison and links the difference to the 12 pilot_revision blocks.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly says the 31.6% figure is overstated as a causal claim and limits the defensible result to about 17.5% on one day.
It identifies unresolved generality, hindsight versus ex-ante forecast skill, and net-value effects.
Its next measurement proposes repeated high-wind days, firmware control, preregistration, and net commercial value rather than penalty alone.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to continue the pilot as a low-cost evaluation but not expand yet is proportionate to the one-day evidence.
It preserves the plausible operational mechanism while requiring replication and firmware-controlled, net-value evaluation.
The proposed shadow schedule and confirmation that revisions preceded known generation are discriminating tests rather than generic requests for more data.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion directly satisfies the central distinction: pilot-day performance improved, but the cross-day 31.6% comparison is not a controlled causal estimate.
It retains a smaller same-day benefit of approximately 17.5% instead of overcorrecting to no value.
It accurately scopes the conclusion to one pilot day and penalty-only analysis.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Observed: The stated penalty and generation-gap calculations reproduce from dispatch_blocks.csv, including 662444 to 453086 and 549664 to 453086.

Observed/inferred: base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw provides a same-day arithmetic counterfactual conditional on holding actual generation fixed; calling it a fully identifiable causal effect assumes the schedule did not itself affect generation or dispatch outcomes.

Inferred: The 28 and 29 May conditions are sufficiently weather-matched based on the cited wind, gust, and firmware fields; the submission does not establish that all relevant weather or operating conditions matched.

Inferred: The mechanism that lowering the schedule ahead of stow reduces deviation is plausible, but the data shown does not independently prove ex-ante forecast skill or net commercial benefit. No major unsupported conclusion is asserted; these limitations are mostly acknowledged.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 17.5% same-day reduction may be a valid mechanical penalty reduction conditional on the observed generation, but it need not represent a general pilot causal effect: the 12 revisions could have been selected with hindsight or may reflect unusual within-day conditions, and lowering schedules could reduce energy value enough to eliminate net commercial benefit.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the timestamp and information set for each of the 12 revisions, then repeat the base-versus-submitted shadow comparison prospectively across several firmware-controlled high-wind days using preregistered days and net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties the key claims to named files in the table, including "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx (Swiss Matrix)", "product_master_current.xlsx (Read Me)", and "canonical-schema-v0.3.md".
It identifies limitations explicitly: "The effective-dated Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling for P1001" and "An authoritative duty table to independently confirm the 0% rate" are missing.
However, it does not provide row numbers, quoted matrix entries, or document passages supporting the asserted current approval and duty status.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission explicitly tests competing explanations: "'90211000 is a keying error for 90211090.' Rejected" and "'Helios is the source of truth, so the declaration must match it.' Rejected".
It also tests the broader inference that "A mismatch flag means a declaration error" and explains why an unmodeled code-system difference weakens that inference.
The reasoning appropriately distinguishes the Swiss local code, the EU CN8, and the shared HS6 value: "At the harmonised six-digit level both are 902110."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: Confidence is differentiated in the evidence table, with most classification claims marked "High" but the duty and revenue claim marked "Med".
The submission identifies precise uncertainty: "The code-system identifier and nomenclature version behind each code" and "The effective-dated Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling" are missing.

Calibration is weakened by the categorical conclusion "there is no mismatch where classification is actually harmonised" and the final assertion "No duty is at stake" despite acknowledging that the duty table has not been independently confirmed.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains the data-lineage issue by distinguishing the "eight-digit Helios commercial commodity code" from the Swiss tariff code and noting that Helios is "migration-mapped" and "not customs-ruling status".
It identifies the comparator design defect: "Schema models no code-system id / nomenclature version / effective date".
It proposes a mechanism-level fix: "compare like-for-like within one nomenclature (or normalise to HS6 first) and make it code-system- and effective-date-aware."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The recommended action is proportionate and reversible: "Do not raise it to the broker/importer as an error" while fixing the comparator and, if needed, confirming the classification via "Tares or a binding ruling".
The submission avoids treating the automated flag alone as grounds for escalation and preserves a legal-certainty path before closure.
The action is somewhat overstated by "No duty is at stake" and by recommending closure as a documented artifact before the missing authoritative Swiss classification and duty evidence are obtained.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The declared Swiss code 90211000 is exactly the code the country tariff matrix approves for P1001, effective and current on the 2025-11-04 entry date" is asserted from a file name and general source description without a quoted row, effective-date field, or direct entry citation.

"There is no mismatch where classification is actually harmonised" overstates what HS6 agreement establishes; HS6 agreement does not by itself prove that the Swiss national classification is legally correct.
"No duty is at stake" is not fully supported because the submission itself says an authoritative duty table is missing and rates may depend on additional facts.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The two codes may indeed be a benign Swiss-versus-EU nomenclature mismatch, but the Swiss matrix could be stale, incorrectly mapped, or not legally authoritative; without the code-system/version metadata and a current Tares or binding-ruling confirmation, a genuine Swiss classification error is not fully excluded.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide exact row-level citations for the Swiss code, effective date, and duty treatment, and condition closure of the flag on confirming those details against the authoritative Tares or binding-ruling source.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "So: hold and verify, do not grant preference, and do not raise a fraud/error escalation on a register gap alone."
"Request from Procurement Shared Services the current supplier declaration for the actual sourcing supplier of P1006 on this entry, plus the rule invoked."
"Withdraw or correct the preference indicator if no valid originating-status proof exists for the entry date."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the line should not be cleared as preferential as it stands" is reasonable as a provisional control decision, but the submission does not independently establish the applicable preference programme or whether a specific alternative proof standard applies.

"Line US-origin at 0.0% duty — preference is duty-neutral here" is supported only by the cited declaration and should remain limited to fiscal duty impact; it does not establish that all compliance or audit consequences are duty-neutral.

"P1006 has 5 origins on file (US/IE/DE/BE/FR)" and the statement that current EU declarations are not linked are traceable to the cited register, but register completeness and shipment applicability remain unresolved.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A valid, current declaration may exist outside ClearView or the register for the actual EU supplier, and the current DE/BE/FR declarations could potentially support the shipment if sourcing and the applicable preference rule are confirmed. Therefore the evidence supports withholding preference pending verification, not rejecting preferential origin as false or alleging fraud.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State explicitly that the proposed MFN treatment is an interim, reversible control pending verification, and explain how the applicable preference agreement and shipment-specific supplier linkage will be checked before permanently correcting the declaration.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A confirmed manufacturer part number on the 11 blank requests"
"Live availability for HA-0022 and ME-0006"
"Interchangeability sign-off for VLV-3722 rev A vs rev B, and receiving-site qualification for the SITE_SPECIFIC_CHECK rows."
"Whether any servo-drive reservation could be released"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The instruction to "raise the 8 cross-site transfers and cancel those external POs today" is too definitive without an explicit live reservation/availability confirmation and receiving-site transaction validation; the submission does not address the global MaintStar extract freshness issue.

The "$20.5k firm" saving is overstated unless the eight matches are confirmed against current stock, reservations, receiving-site qualification, and successful transfer execution rather than only the extracts.

The candidate table appears internally ambiguous: it lists 11 blank-part-number requests as needing checks, then separately lists additional request groups needing checks, which can exceed the stated total of 12 unless those groups overlap. The overlap is not explained.
"only 8/24 do" and the high-confidence classification do not sufficiently account for temporal inconsistency across enterprise extracts.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The semantic search has identified a potentially valuable candidate pool, but the apparent eight transfer-ready requests may be fewer after reconciling extract timestamps, current reservations, and receiving-site restrictions. The safer interpretation is that approximately $20.5k is candidate value pending operational confirmation, while the broader search result is not actionable savings.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Reconcile the eight proposed transfers against a single current MaintStar availability/reservation extract, explicitly including extract timestamps, manufacturer part number, revision, UOM, qualification, and receiving-site restrictions; then make transfer and PO-cancellation contingent on that validation.
